headline: Jensen Huang pitches containerised AI factories and an agent sandbox in Berlin; Russia frees American Stephen Hubbard as Witkoff meets Putin; the PHP fix is still due at 16:00; Emma closes after 50 years.

stories.title: Jensen Huang in Berlin: containerised AI factories, a sandbox for AI agents, and a Greenpeace interruption
facts: Huang gave the GTC Berlin keynote at the Tempodrom this morning; the conference runs Oct 20–22 with more than 100 sessions.
DSX POD: partner-built Vera Rubin AI factories delivered in pre-validated modular containers; NVIDIA says on-site deployment drops from six months to 14 days once power and cooling are ready.
NVIDIA claims its DSX designs cut cooling water use by up to 100% and need up to 30% less power for the same output; DCD says DSX POD sites are due worldwide from early 2027.
OpenShell Reference Architecture: an open-source runtime that sandboxes AI agents and enforces policy outside the agent, with Gateway, Supervisor, Sandbox and Policy Prover parts.
With BlueField-4 chips and NVIDIA Sentry, NVIDIA says agents that break policy can be quarantined within milliseconds.
Minutes in, Greenpeace activists interrupted, asking about Nvidia Jetson chips found in Russian drones; Huang: "I'll talk to you later."
Also announced: Isaac robotics tools with a reference humanoid, telecom AI deals with Nokia and operators, and Hyperion for European carmakers' robotaxi fleets.
NVIDIA says it is committing nearly $10bn to Europe's tech ecosystem.
stories.whyItMatters: The Europe pitch is less about chips than about building AI data centres faster with less water and power, plus a safety layer for agents that NVIDIA wants to become the standard.

stories.title: Russia frees American Stephen Hubbard as Witkoff meets Putin in St. Petersburg
facts: Putin said during his talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff that Russia has released Stephen Hubbard, 74, a former teacher from Michigan (BBC, citing state media).

Hubbard was captured in Ukraine in 2022 and sentenced in 2024 to almost seven years in a penal colony, accused of serving in a defence unit in Izyum; the State Department called him wrongfully detained.
He was taken to Pulkovo airport and is due to fly back to the US with Witkoff (ZEIT).
Trump says he asked Putin for the release; the NYT notes it comes as Putin has scored wins with Trump.
Zelensky, after another meeting with Norway's Støre in Oslo this morning: "A lot depends on whether the American side manages to hear something new from Russia today."
stories.whyItMatters: A goodwill gesture at the start of the talks on the plan worked out in Oslo; nothing has come out yet on the substance.

stories.title: PHP fix still due at 16:00, and the UK's NCSC joins the "take it offline if you can't patch" advice
facts: As of lunchtime php.net still shows only the advance notice; the fixes for both CVSS 9.2 flaws are due at 14:00 UTC (16:00 Berlin), possibly earlier.
The UK's NCSC published an alert: find every PHP system, watch internet-facing ones for malicious activity, and consider taking a system offline if you can't fix it right away.
It also says to watch for updates from vendors whose appliances and services bundle PHP.
Australia's ACSC issued similar guidance and says it isn't aware of active exploitation (RTÉ, via Reuters).
stories.whyItMatters: If you run PHP anywhere, the release lands this afternoon; vendor-bundled PHP will lag behind php.net.

stories.title: Alice Schwarzer shuts down "Emma" after 50 years
facts: The feminist magazine will publish its last issue on 8 December, Schwarzer announced.
"Wir meinen, es reicht," she said; according to ZDF, money was not the deciding reason.
Schwarzer, 83, founded Emma almost 50 years ago.

facts.text: BGH on Schufa scores: Schufa must explain how a score is built only if a company's contract decision hinged on it, which a refusal soon after a score was sent lets courts presume. Four cases go back to Dresden.
Berlin: the SPD, Greens and Left want people who have lived in Germany for five years to vote even without a German passport; there is no concrete legal route yet.
UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, a bit above forecasts, driven by fuel and airfares; government debt passed £3tn ahead of next week's Budget.
Subaru will sell only electric cars in Europe by the end of 2027, citing EU emissions and driver-assistance rules.
Australian MP Helen Haines has lost both legs after an alleged deliberate car attack; the 43-year-old accused appeared in court on Wednesday.
The EU Commission opened proceedings against Booking.com over fake listings and other risks.
German regional transport associations are running out of money; first connections have been cut, with more possibly to follow.
Cursor: cloud agents can now build and share interactive canvases; the Environments API is in beta, environments take up to 300 repos and large ones load 5x faster.
Anthropic's Claude Code team on reviewing code at agent volume: once coverage was high, they optimised for the least human review time that doesn't raise reverts or incidents.
Vercel AI Gateway October index: open-weight models take 71.5% of tokens but only 23% of spend.
Bun merged a --hardened=on build option: stack protector, _FORTIFY_SOURCE, stack-clash protection and zeroed locals across the board.
Vite v8.3.5 fixes chunk import maps (missing maps, preload dependencies in hashing).
Josh W. Comeau picks his top 10 CSS features for Interop 2027, which Mozilla is ranking by votes.
Firefox asks developers to hold back tests for security fixes until the fixes ship, for at least a week.
Jake Archibald: in browsers, JPEG and AVIF support HDR gain maps and JPEG XL doesn't.
